content:
incident-bot: ALERT: SLO breach detected for /v1/stream (p99 latency 12.1s, SLO 2.0s) — paging oncall
sara: acked, I'm oncall for this rotation
mike: paging in, seeing mobile clients report stalled streams
sara: giving context: p95 jumped from ~350ms -> 3.2s, p99 from 1.8s -> 12.1s in us-west-2
ops-bot: Event details: 2026-03-15T14:24:28Z | route:/v1/stream | p95=3.2s p99=12.1s error_rate=0.6% | affected_hosts=gpu-nd-042,gpu-nd-043
tess: looking at runtime traces — many streaming sessions stalling around token ~512 with repeated retries in kernel loop
sara: which nodes show hardware signals?
ops-bot: gpu-nd-042: GPU temp=92C, fan=100%, ECC_correctable=12/min, power_draw=320W; gpu-nd-043: temp=78C, ECC_correctable=1/min
jordan: gpu-nd-042 looks suspect — ECC and thermal both high. Could be thermal throttle -> kernel slowdowns -> streaming tail stalls
mike: can we start live mitigation: drain and isolate the node, route new sessions off it, enable fallback path for long-lived streams
sara: doing steps now: 1) isolate node 2) drain active streams 3) toggle fallback routing to quantized/cpu variants
sara: `rdctl node drain gpu-nd-042 --reason "thermal/ecc live mitigation"`
ops-bot: drain command accepted. Active sessions: 128 (streaming: 73). Draining -> initiating graceful handoff
tess: enabling routing change: `route set /v1/stream fallback_variant=compact-quant --immediate true` -> new requests should hit fallback pool
mike: request infra to scale fallback pool: `infra scale pool fallback-cpu +10`
jordan: scaling requested, ETA ~95s. Monitoring autoscaling events
ops-bot: drain progress: 73 streaming sessions -> 38 remaining -> 12 remaining -> draining slow sessions may take time (clients with no reconnect)
sara: customer impact: short stalls and reconnects observed for a small percentage of requests. Early estimate: ~0.3% of total QPS since spike; affected customers include a couple of heavy-streaming tenants
mike: runtime logs showing repeated cuda kernel soft-failures on stream 3 preceding stalls: `serving/runtime: stream stall trace` -> stack snippets attached in logs
sara: contacting ENG-HW: @alex can you join? we need BMC/NVML logs and advise on quarantining node
alex: on it. pulling BMC syslogs and nvml traces now. initial look: sustained thermal throttle state starting ~14:18Z and increasing ECC correctable error rate from baseline
alex: opening vendor support case VEND-2026-7321, will include GPU serial and power logs. Recommend hardware quarantine pending replacement/further benching
tess: noting mitigation actions in incident tracker: route fallback enabled, node gpu-nd-042 drained and isolated, fallback pool scaled +10
mike: do we have a live workaround for active sessions that are already slow? Suggest automatic CPU fallback for sessions exceeding Xs/token
sara: agree. enabling temporary flag: `featureflag enable cpu-stream-fallback --expires 30m` to move long-tail sessions to CPU slow-stream path when token latency >6s
jordan: rolling canary: 5% traffic to fallback CPU for 2m -> no regressions -> increase to 25%
ops-bot: Canary at 5% for 2m: OK. Increasing to 25% now
sara: drafting customer-facing impacted list and escalation notes. Notifying account teams for tenants with sustained connections
mike: host quarantine steps: mark node cordoned in scheduler, remove from load balancer slowly to avoid mass reconnect storms
alex: cordoned and quarantined in hardware inventory. Serial: GPU-SN-89B2; chassis PSU logs show intermittent power spikes that align with thermal events
tess: adding alert rule: ECC_correctable_rate >= 5/min for 5m -> page hw oncall (new rule), and lower threshold for streaming route p99 to trigger earlier mitigation
sara: perf update: p99 reduced to ~3.0s after routing and canary increase; by 14:45Z sample p99=1.9s, error rate back to baseline
ops-bot: Mitigation actions recorded: drain gpu-nd-042; route fallback enabled; fallback pool scaled; cpu-stream-fallback enabled; vendor ticket opened
mike: next steps: vendor replacement schedule, bench the node for flake, update runbook to include auto-fallback earlier in flow (e.g., p99 > 3s for 2m)
jordan: I'll own the postmortem — will gather timeline, root cause (probable hardware thermal-triggered ECC bursts) and action items (alert tuning, hw replacement, runbook update)
sara: summary for handoff: incident MITIGATED for live traffic, ongoing hw remediation. RTO estimate for full resolution: 45-60m (replacement coordinate)
alex: vendor replied, aligning on replacement window; sending parts request now
tess: final check: dashboard 14:52Z sample p95=420ms p99=1.9s, streaming sessions stable
sara: marking this thread as mitigation-complete. Postmortem owner @jordan to file followup. Thanks all :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident logged: https://redwood.incidents/1799002468 — status: mitigated (live), followup: postmortem scheduled
jordan: taking postmortem ownership, will ping for timelines and link once created
